title: Go up to Nahargarh for sunset, not Amber
text: Everyone queues at Amber Fort in the morning. Nahargarh Fort on the ridge above the city is quieter and the view over the whole pink city at sunset is the better photograph. Take a cab up, walk down.

title: Eat where the locals queue
text: Skip the hotel buffet and eat pyaaz kachori and lassi in the old city lanes near Johari Bazaar. Go before noon, the good places sell out.

title: Buy your fort tickets as a composite pass
text: There is a combined ticket covering several monuments over two days. If you plan to see more than two forts it is far cheaper than paying at each gate.

title: The cheap boat is the city bus of the lake
text: Instead of the expensive tourist cruise, take the shared ferry across Lake Pichola. Same water, same views, a fraction of the price.

title: Rooftop cafes at Hanuman Ghat
text: The west bank of the lake has small rooftop cafes where you can sit for hours with a chai and a view of the City Palace. Sunset seats fill by 5pm.

title: Walk the blue city early
text: The blue houses under Mehrangarh look best in the first hour of light and the lanes are empty. By ten it is hot and full of tour groups.

title: Sleep inside the fort or outside, not both
text: The living fort has guesthouses inside, which is atmospheric but the water pressure is bad. Staying just outside the gate is cheaper and you still walk in every evening.

title: South Goa if you want quiet
text: North Goa beaches are loud and packed. Palolem, Agonda and Patnem in the south are calmer, cheaper off season, and better for swimming.

title: Rent a scooter, not a taxi
text: Goa taxis are famously expensive and there is very little public transport. A scooter for the day costs less than one taxi ride and makes the whole trip cheaper.

title: Eat at a beach shack at lunch
text: The same fish thali costs much less at lunch than at dinner in the tourist strips, and the catch is fresher earlier in the day.

title: Old Goa churches on a weekday
text: The Portuguese-era churches inland are free to enter and almost empty on weekday mornings. It is a completely different side of Goa from the beaches.

title: Old Manali versus Mall Road
text: Mall Road is the tourist centre. Old Manali up the hill has the cafes, the cheaper guesthouses and the river. Stay there if you are travelling on a budget.

title: Check if the pass is open before you plan it
text: Rohtang and the higher passes close with snow and need a permit that sells out. Ask your guesthouse the night before instead of booking a cab blind.

title: Cross the river for quiet
text: Kasol itself has become busy. The villages across the bridge are a short walk away, much quieter, and have the same mountain views.

title: The toy train is the journey
text: The narrow gauge line up to Shimla is slow and that is the point. Book a window seat in advance, it fills up in season.

title: Free evening aarti at the ghats
text: The riverside evening ceremony costs nothing, happens daily around sunset, and is the most memorable thing many travellers do here.

title: Rafting is cheapest booked in town
text: Booking a rafting stretch through a hotel adds a big margin. The operators on the main road quote much lower for exactly the same trip.

title: Use it as a base, not a destination
text: Dehradun itself is a small city, but Mussoorie, Rishikesh and Haridwar are all short drives away. Stay here, spend your days outside it.

title: Walk the Camel's Back Road at dawn
text: This loop road is closed to most traffic and quiet in the early morning, with clear views of the Doon valley before the haze sets in.

title: Take the dawn boat, skip the sunset one
text: The morning boat along the ghats is calmer, cooler, and the light is better. Agree the price before you get in.

title: Get lost in the lanes on purpose
text: The old lanes are impossible to navigate by map and that is the best way to see them. Note your ghat's name so you can always ask your way back.

title: See the Taj from the other bank
text: Mehtab Bagh across the river gives you the same monument at sunset with a fraction of the crowd and a much cheaper ticket.

title: Agra Fort is worth a full morning
text: Most people rush it in forty minutes on the way to the Taj. It deserves longer, and it is far less crowded.

title: The metro beats every taxi
text: Delhi traffic is brutal and the metro is clean, air conditioned and cheap. Buy a tourist card for unlimited rides if you are staying more than two days.

title: Lodhi Garden in the morning
text: Free, full of medieval tombs, and locals treat it as a park rather than a monument. A good quiet start before the city wakes up.

title: Local train outside rush hour
text: The suburban trains are the fastest way across the city, but avoid 8-11am and 5-9pm unless you enjoy being compressed.

title: Bandra street art walk
text: The lanes of Bandra West are covered in murals and cost nothing to walk. Best in the late afternoon when it cools down.

title: Fort Kochi is walkable, the rest is not
text: Base yourself in Fort Kochi and do everything on foot. Ernakulam across the water is where the buses and trains are, connected by a cheap ferry.

title: A day boat instead of an overnight houseboat
text: Overnight houseboats are the expensive option. A shared day cruise or a small canoe through the narrow canals shows you more of actual village life.

title: Go early or the mist wins
text: The tea estate viewpoints cloud over by late morning for much of the year. Leave your stay by six if you want the view.

title: Cliff top for views, beach for swimming
text: The cliff has the cafes and the sunsets. The swimming is better and safer at the main beach below and at the quieter northern stretch.

title: Cross the river to the Hippie Island side
text: The main bazaar side has the ruins, the other bank has the cheap guesthouses and the paddy fields. A small ferry runs across during daylight.

title: Cycle the ruins, do not walk them
text: The site is spread over kilometres of rock and heat. A bicycle or a scooter for the day turns an exhausting trip into a good one.

title: Stay on a homestay, not a resort
text: The coffee estate homestays are cheaper than the resorts, include home cooked food, and the owners will walk you through the plantation themselves.

title: The French quarter is small, so slow down
text: You can walk the whole coloured-street grid in an hour. The point is to sit in it, not to tick it off. Mornings are best before the heat.

title: Tiger Hill sunrise is a convoy
text: Hundreds of jeeps leave at 4am for the same viewpoint. If you want the mountain without the crowd, ask about the smaller viewpoints on the same ridge.

title: Permits take a day, plan for it
text: Several areas beyond Gangtok need a permit arranged through a registered agent. Build a buffer day into the plan rather than losing your booked trip.

title: Give yourself two days to acclimatise
text: Flying straight in and driving high the next day is how people get altitude sickness. The first two days should be flat and slow. This is not optional.

title: Eat at the langar
text: The community kitchen at the Golden Temple serves free food to anyone, all day. Volunteering in the washing-up line is a genuinely good experience.

title: Sunrise on the beach, temple in the evening
text: The fishing beach at dawn is the local scene rather than the tourist one. Note that the main temple restricts entry for non-Hindus.

title: The living root bridges need a full day
text: The double decker bridge is thousands of steps down and the same back up. Treat it as a trek, not a stop, and start early.

title: The lake is skippable, the tea estates are not
text: The boating lake is the most crowded thing in town. The estate roads outside the centre are where the actual scenery is.

title: Weekends double the price
text: Being a weekend escape from Delhi, room rates jump Friday to Sunday. Arriving Monday to Thursday can halve your stay cost.

title: Ferries book out, book them first
text: Inter-island ferries sell out days ahead in season. Lock the ferries before you lock the hotels, because the ferry decides your itinerary.

title: Only summer, and cash only
text: The road is snowed shut much of the year and ATMs are almost nonexistent once you are inside the valley. Carry cash and check the road status.
